text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A Council of Europe monitoring group said it was happy with the conduct of the second round of local polls.
- Council of Europe delegation head Andreas Gross said he believed Albania should hold fresh parliamentary elections.
- The ethnic Greek Union for Human Rights Party has lost its dominant position both in the municipality and district council of the southern Gjirokastra region, home to the ethnic Greek community.
- A Socialist vice chairman at a polling station in the region of Mirdite is recovering from a gun wound allegedly inflicted by a fellow Democratic Party commissioner.

- The ruling Democratic Party says it won 21 out of 22 municipalities and 73 out of 96 communes in the second round of local elections. Over the two rounds the Democrats have won 90 percent of the municipalities and 86 percent of the communes.
- The opposition Socialist Party said the local eletions were not free and fair.
- A candidate from a coalition of monarchists and the nationalists, two rightist parties, managed to win the seat of mayor of the northern town of Shkoder from the Democrats.

- The Albanian government has approved a draft law requiring traders to present to customs purchase documents and receipts for goods. The measure is aimed at curbing tax evasion but is likely to increase prices.
- Albania's battle to get back gold held in the Bank of England is likely to end following talks in London between the two governments.
- The paper said the victory of the ruling Democrats in municipal polls spelled the disintegration of the opposition Socialist Party.
